findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The cleanup loop now runs every minute instead of every 10 minutes. The change looks like leftover debugging and is unrelated to the deadlock fix. It runs all cleanup jobs 10x as often, which adds DB load and increases the chance of overlapping with the 9-minute timeout. The previous value should be restored.

findings.title: Debug logging at Error level with full ID lists
findings.body: Each batch logs at Error level, including the entire ID slice (up to batch size, e.g. 32767 IDs) and the condition. This runs on every cleanup iteration, even on success. It floods the error logs, triggers alerts, and is very large. The same pattern appears at lines 537, 554, 557, 576 and 579. These should be removed or lowered to Debug without the ID lists.

findings.title: Orphaned tag cleanup selects a non-existent id column
findings.body: fetchIDs runs `SELECT id FROM annotation_tag`, but annotation_tag has no id column in the Grafana schema (it has annotation_id and tag_id; the old code also used id, so this may need verifying). If the column is absent the query errors and orphan cleanup fails. The unqualified `annotation_id` in the NOT EXISTS subquery is also ambiguous.

findings.title: SQLite parameter-limit workaround keyed on config, not actual id count
findings.body: The 999 limit applies to the number of parameters, and modern SQLite allows 32766. The branch inlines IDs only when the configured batch size exceeds 999. This is functionally safe, but it uses string concatenation in a loop that is O(n^2) for large batches (32767 IDs). A strings.Builder would be better.

findings.title: Max-count cleanup with OFFSET and the loop termination
findings.body: Each iteration re-fetches with LIMIT batch OFFSET maxCount. This works only because deleted rows shift the window. It also makes the type filter `annotationType` interpolated into SQL unescaped, as before. If a delete affects fewer rows than were fetched, for example from concurrent deletion, the loop can end early. Under-deletion is acknowledged in the comment, but affected==0 with non-empty ids also ends the loop silently.
